info.title: SiteScope API
info.summary: Distributed web crawling and search infrastructure.

get.description: Describe the service and link to the API, health, and documentation endpoints.

Return 200 while the process is able to serve requests.

This is a liveness check only. It does not check PostgreSQL, Redis, or any other dependency.

Confirm that the API process is running and its event loop is serving requests.

It reports only the process's own state and checks no external dependency.

Check PostgreSQL (``SELECT 1``) and Redis (``PING``) under a short deadline.

Returns 200 only when both respond. Otherwise returns 503 with the same body shape.

503.description: PostgreSQL or Redis is unavailable; the body says which.

post.description:
Validate the request and store the job with its seed URL, in one transaction.

The seed URL is normalized and must name an approved crawl target; `max_depth` and
`max_pages` must be within this server's limits. The job is created as `queued`: it waits
for the scheduler, and nothing is fetched yet. The `Location` header points to the job.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Optional. 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters. Retrying a request with the same key and an equivalent body returns the job the first request created (`200`) instead of creating another; the same key with a different body is a `409 idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are remembered for SITESCOPE_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TTL_SECONDS.
schema.title: Idempotency-Key

parameters.description: Optional. 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters. Retrying a request with the same key and an equivalent body returns the job the first request created (`200`) instead of creating another; the same key with a different body is a `409 idempotency_key_reused`. Keys are remembered for SITESCOPE_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_TTL_SECONDS.

200.description: A replay: an earlier request with the same `Idempotency-Key` and an equivalent body created this job (header `Idempotent-Replayed: true`).

409.description: The request conflicts with earlier ones: an `Idempotency-Key` reused for a different request (`idempotency_key_reused`).

422.description: The request failed validation (`validation_failed`); `errors` lists each field.

get.description:
List crawl jobs, newest first, with cursor (keyset) pagination.

Paging never returns a job twice, and returns every job that existed when paging started.
Jobs created meanwhile do not shift later pages.

422.description: The request failed validation (`validation_failed`); `errors` lists each field.

post.description:
Cancel a job. Idempotent: repeating it, or cancelling a finished job, changes nothing.

A `queued` job is `cancelled` at once (`200`). A `running` job stops: nothing new is
dispatched or claimed, and its pending and queued URLs are cancelled at once. If none of its
URLs is in progress, it is `cancelled` at once (`200`); otherwise it is `cancelling` (`202`)
until its in-flight URLs are final (workers stop them within seconds; the URLs of a crashed
worker are cancelled when their lease expires). The response is `202` whenever the job is
still `cancelling`, and `200` with the unchanged job for a finished one (`completed`,
`failed`, `cancelled`).

202.description: The job is `cancelling`: in-flight URLs are still finishing.

422.description: The request failed validation (`validation_failed`); `errors` lists each field.

get.description:
Return the crawl targets this server approves and its job limits.

A seed URL is accepted when its host matches an approved pattern and its scheme and port
are allowed (schemes and ports apply to every approved host), and `max_depth` and
`max_pages` are within the limits. The server checks every request again: this is
guidance for clients, not a promise that a URL can be crawled.

get.summary: List the pages of a crawl job
get.description:
List the job's stored HTML pages in BFS order (depth, then URL), with cursor paging.

A *page* is an HTML document the crawl fetched (2xx) and stored. Other crawled URLs
(redirects, errors, other content types) are not pages; the links and statistics endpoints
report them. Page bodies are never returned.

get.summary: List the links of a crawl job
get.description:
List the job's stored links, by source page URL and position, with their classification.

Every link found on a stored page is recorded, internal or not, followed or not. A link's
classification comes from this job's stored crawl result for its target (after the
target's redirects); a target that was never requested is never reported as working or
broken. Nothing is fetched to check a link.

get.summary: List the confirmed broken links of a crawl job
get.description:
List the job's confirmed broken links, by target URL, then source page URL.

A link is *confirmed broken* when it is internal and its target, after following its
redirects through this job's crawl results, answered 404 Not Found or 410 Gone during this
crawl. Nothing else is: not a 5xx, 408 or 429 (possibly transient), not another 4xx such as
401 or 403, not a link the crawl never requested (out of scope, nofollow, beyond the depth
or page limits, blocked by robots.txt, not crawled yet), and not one that got no response.
Those are in the links listing, by classification.

One item per stored link: a page that links to a missing URL twice is listed once; a URL
linked from three pages is listed three times. `total` counts every item.

get.summary: Get the internal link graph of a crawl job
get.description:
Return the job's internal link graph: its known URLs, and the stored internal links
between them.

Nodes are every URL the job admitted (pages, and URLs without a page) and every target of
an internal link the job never admitted, in BFS order; `kind` tells them apart. The graph
is cut at `max_nodes` and `max_edges` in a stable order, and `truncated` says so.

The graph holds only what the crawl stored: links on pages it did not fetch are unknown, so
a node without inbound links is not necessarily an orphan page.

get.description:
Return the job's crawl, HTTP status, depth, indexing and link statistics.

Every number is counted from stored rows in one snapshot of PostgreSQL: nothing is

get.summary: Search the pages of one crawl job
get.description:
Search the indexed pages of one crawl job, ranked by relevance.

Only pages whose current content is indexed are found: a page that is not indexed yet, or
whose index is older than its content, is not returned, and nothing else (pages of other
jobs, unindexed text) is ever searched instead. While the job is still crawling or
indexing (`indexing.status` is `pending` or `running`), a later search may find more.

Results are ordered by score, then URL, then page ID, so pages do not overlap or skip
results while the index is unchanged. `total` counts every match. Every match is ranked
before a page is cut, which is why results are served up to offset 1000 only.

parameters.name: job_id

schema.description: The crawl job to search. A search never covers another job.
schema.title: Job Id

parameters.description: The crawl job to search. A search never covers another job.

parameters.name: q

schema.description: The query, in web-search syntax: words (all must match), quoted `"exact phrases"`, `or` between alternatives, and `-word` to exclude a word. At most 256 characters after invisible characters are removed and whitespace is collapsed. Words are matched by their English stem (`crawling` finds `crawled`); stop words such as `the` are ignored.
schema.title: Q

parameters.description: The query, in web-search syntax: words (all must match), quoted `"exact phrases"`, `or` between alternatives, and `-word` to exclude a word. At most 256 characters after invisible characters are removed and whitespace is collapsed. Words are matched by their English stem (`crawling` finds `crawled`); stop words such as `the` are ignored.

parameters.name: page

schema.description: 1-based page number. A search serves results up to offset 1000: a page with `(page - 1) * page_size` above it is refused (`page_out_of_range`).
schema.title: Page

parameters.description: 1-based page number. A search serves results up to offset 1000: a page with `(page - 1) * page_size` above it is refused (`page_out_of_range`).

422.description: The request failed validation (`validation_failed`); `errors` lists each field with its `type`: `empty_query` (nothing left after removing whitespace and invisible characters), `query_too_long`, `page_out_of_range` (reported together with a query error), or a schema rule (for example `uuid_parsing` for `job_id`, `missing` for a missing parameter).

503.description: The search took longer than SITESCOPE_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and was stopped (`search_timeout`), or PostgreSQL is unavailable (`dependency_unavailable`, with `Retry-After`).

get.summary: Get the overview of every crawl job
get.description:
Count every crawl job by status, every admitted URL by state, the stored pages and the
search documents by status, in one read-only snapshot of PostgreSQL.

Each count reads every row of its table, so the time grows with the deployment's data; it
is stopped after SITESCOPE_ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. Discovered URLs (admitted ones plus
link targets never admitted) are counted per job, in its statistics.

503.description: The counts took longer than SITESCOPE_ANALYSIS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS and were stopped (`analysis_timeout`), or PostgreSQL is unavailable (`dependency_unavailable`, with `Retry-After`).

query.title: Query

searchable.title: Searchable
searchable.description: False when the query has no term an index can look up, for example only stop words (`the and`) or only excluded words (`-redis`): nothing was searched, and there are no results.

tags.name: analysis
tags.description: Read-only analysis of one crawl job, from its stored results in PostgreSQL; nothing is fetched again. Terms: a *URL* is *discovered* when the job admitted it or a stored page links to it (internally); *admitted* URLs are crawled (or skipped) by the job. A *page* is a fetched HTML document (2xx) the job stored. A *link* is one stored link from a page to a target URL. A *broken link* is an internal link whose target, after its redirects, answered 404 or 410 during the crawl; a link is *unverified* when no HTTP response decides it (never requested, or no response). A *document* is a page's search-index entry (none for `noindex` pages). Details: ADR-0019.

tags.description: Full-text search of one crawl job's indexed pages (PostgreSQL full-text search, ranked with `ts_rank`).
